video_title: Post Game Media Availability | Preseason | October 6, 2026 | OKC Thunder

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams praises the team's defensive potential
quotes.excerpt: he feels like we have all-defensive first or second team potential
quotes.quote: It feels good to hear that from him. He is an experienced player, so he has been in this league a lot of years. I think it is going to take time. This is my first NBA preseason game. I still need to learn a lot of things, play against a lot of players, and get better and better. That really helps me to work better with more energy, knowing that if he thinks that way, it is because maybe he knows something.
quotes.social_post: A rookie reflects on his first NBA preseason game and the value of veteran leadership. He says it is going to take time to learn the ropes but he is focused on working with energy.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: The origin of the nickname Big Spain
quotes.excerpt: Last year I was the Big Coof, now I am the Big Spain
quotes.quote: Last year I was the Big Coof, now I am the Big Spain, so I am like big something. I like it. He told me he knew some Spanish from high school or when he was younger. He is always telling me the same thing, un poquito, un poquito. Everyone is saying un poquito, they always say un poquito. Maybe I got that nickname this year or they will find something else.
quotes.social_post: From Big Coof to Big Spain. A lighthearted moment from the Thunder locker room as a player discusses his new nickname and his teammates learning to say un poquito.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: How veteran teammates have helped the transition to the NBA
quotes.excerpt: having them in the team, for me the role is way easier
quotes.quote: Having them in the team, for me the role is way easier to what it was last year. It is more basic stuff, more easy stuff, like rebounding or setting screens. I feel that I don't have that pressure that maybe I had in Michigan, for example. That makes it easier to get to a game knowing that you have to do basic things right now.
quotes.social_post: Transitioning to the NBA is easier when you have veterans around. A Thunder player says his role is much more basic than it was in college, allowing him to focus on rebounding and setting screens without the pressure.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: The team's offensive flow and shooting performance
quotes.excerpt: we shot 65% from three in the first half, that's not realistic
quotes.quote: We were in a good little rhythm. We shot 65% from three in the first half, that's not realistic. That's probably above expectation, although I thought we got good looks. We had a nice pop to us, so I was pleased with how we came out after a week of camping. You never know what it's going to look like on either end of the floor and I thought we were pretty sharp, obviously, to start that game.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault was pleased with the Thunder's sharp start to the preseason. He noted the team shot 65 percent from three in the first half, admitting that is not realistic but praising the rhythm and good looks.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: The team's shared philosophy across veteran and young players
quotes.excerpt: one of the things that's been great about this team is just the like-mindedness of all the players
quotes.quote: One of the things that's been great about this team is just the like-mindedness of all the players, from K-Rich and Caruso that are early 30s players to the guys that are in the thick of their 20s and to the young guys. It's a group of guys that are professional, they're competitive, they play inside the team, they're hungry and committed, and it's top to bottom, regardless of anyone's place on the team or in the league.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault highlights the like-mindedness of the Thunder roster. He says the group is professional, competitive, and committed from top to bottom, regardless of experience level.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the rookie's transition to playing off the ball
quotes.excerpt: moving off the ball is a little new for him
quotes.quote: He is used to having the ball in his hands. He was the highest usage player in college basketball last year, and so moving off the ball is a little new for him. During the week you could see him trying to calibrate the balance of aggression when he's got the ball in his hands and functionality. Today was actually his best day, despite the fact that it was a game day. He took the right shots, he attacked on the right plays, he kept it moving on the right ones on offense.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the rookie transition: He is used to having the ball in his hands, so moving off the ball is new. Daigneault says today was his best day yet in terms of taking the right shots and keeping the offense moving.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: The rookie's physical conditioning and work ethic
quotes.excerpt: he worked really hard from the end of Summer League till he came back to Oklahoma City
quotes.quote: He worked really hard from the end of Summer League till he came back to Oklahoma City, and then to the start of training camp in Oklahoma City. That's a lot of days that he stacked up with his head down on his body and on his conditioning, and it showed up tonight. He's obviously a very effective player because of the skill level on offense and then the impact on defense, but you have to be in great shape to do those things.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault credits the rookie's conditioning for his strong performance tonight. He says the player stacked up a lot of days with his head down working on his body after Summer League.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: The rookie's quiet improvement and understanding of the NBA game
quotes.excerpt: he's quietly gotten a lot better year over year
quotes.quote: He's quietly gotten a lot better year over year. If you look at him compared to last year, he just has a much better understanding of the NBA game, our system, his game. It's hard when you're a young player, all these guys that are new, learning all those things all at once is difficult. It's not like it's progressive, you don't get to do one at a time, it all hits you in the face all at once.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault says the rookie has quietly gotten a lot better year over year, showing a much better understanding of the NBA game and the team system.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: The rookie's likability and positive impact on teammates
quotes.quote: I can't speak for the masses, I certainly can't speak for young fans, I'm 41, but he's a very likable guy. That's what I can say. He's a very likable guy and what you see is what he is. He is comfortable in his own skin, he's like that every day. He's endeared himself to his teammates, and I can only speak inside of our walls.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the rookie's personality: He is a very likable guy who is comfortable in his own skin. He has endeared himself to his teammates inside the walls of the organization.
